divine command theory as a constitutive claim with its four-step argument and the three presuppositions, of which Kant denies only the third; the Euthyphro at 10a in both horns with the vacuity consequence that empties divine goodness; modified divine command (Adams's obligation/goodness split, Alston's supreme-standard reply, Zagzebski's divine motivation theory) with the residual concession of conceptual independence, which the Advanced dossier's promotion ledger of 15 August 2026 confirms is Core and not Advanced-only; Kantian autonomy, the autonomy/heteronomy fork, the practical postulates and the formalism reply; natural law as the mediating position with the nature-to-norm objection and the goods-as-reasons answer; the four secular groundings with their four distinct bills; the interaction view split into religion's five influence mechanisms behind the causal-influence-is-not-dependence wall and morality's criticism of religion through the six tests of a claimed command, the prophetic critique, the ethical-fruits test, the plural-moralities block and the internal-corruption reply;
